issues.title: Incorrect Revenue Calculation
issues.problem: The query sums all transaction amounts without filtering for 'COMPLETED' status.
issues.fix: SUM(CASE WHEN b.status = 'COMPLETED' THEN b.amount ELSE 0 END) AS s

issues.title: Correlated Subquery
issues.problem: The correlated subquery can be inefficient as it runs for each row in the result set.
issues.fix: LEFT JOIN a subquery with pre-aggregated failed counts.

issues.title: Implicit Join Syntax
issues.line: FROM dim_customer a, fact_transactions b, dim_merchant c
issues.problem: Implicit join syntax is less readable and more prone to errors.
issues.fix: Use explicit JOIN syntax for better readability.

issues.title: Lack of Comments
issues.problem: The query lacks comments explaining the logic, especially around the revenue calculation and failure rate.
issues.fix: Add comments explaining the logic of the query.

review.corrected_sql:
WITH failed_transactions AS (
  SELECT x.customer_id, COUNT(*) AS failed_count
  FROM fact_transactions x
  WHERE x.status = 'FAILED'
  GROUP BY x.customer_id
)
SELECT a.customer_name,
       a.email,
       a.tier,
       a.city,
       SUM(CASE WHEN b.status = 'COMPLETED' THEN b.amount ELSE 0 END) AS revenue,
       COALESCE(f.failed_count, 0) AS failed_count
FROM dim_customer a
JOIN fact_transactions b ON a.customer_id = b.customer_id
JOIN dim_merchant c ON b.merchant_id = c.merchant_id
LEFT JOIN failed_transactions f ON a.customer_id = f.customer_id
WHERE c.category = 'Food Delivery'
GROUP BY a.customer_name, a.email, a.tier, a.city, a.customer_id
ORDER BY revenue DESC;
review.summary: The query had issues with revenue calculation, performance due to a correlated subquery, readability with implicit joins, and lacked comments.
